items.title: Urbie Green interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995
items.q: I was working with Benny around New York in some small combo kinds of things like at Basin Street West. Teddy Wilson was playing with him at the time

ctx.x: Is that, what’s it like to do a film like that, is it you sit around and wait a lot?

Well, Benny, I was working with Benny around New York in some small combo kinds of things like at Basin Street West. Teddy Wilson was playing with him at the time and Paul Quinchette, Ruby Braff, and he had, I had just signed on as CBS as a staff musician there and Benny asked me if I’d like to go to California to do a soundtrack for “The Benny Goodman Story.” And I really wanted to do it, so I went and got a release from the CBS and I never had a steady job after that, that was the last steady job ever, which is…
couple of weeks. We just pretended to be playing because we’d already made the soundtrack.

items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: he had Urbie Green in the trombone section

ctx.x: But the movie band was a great band; he had Stan Getz in the reed section, because during a lot of the solo work and in the smaller groups doing solo, he had Urbie Green in the trombone section, the soundtrack, and also photographed along with some of the small group sessions. Of course, the original quartet was in the movie -- Lionel was there and Gene Krupa and myself, and we were all photographed because we did our own sound tracks. And I'm trying to think if there was anyone else that you know very well who…
Did Benny's brother go out there at all?
